study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Kia SM et al., PLoS ONE, 2022
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Closing the life-cycle of normative modeling using federated hierarchical Bayesian regression

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Federated probabilistic framework using hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we introduce a federated probabilistic framework using hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) to complete the life-cycle of normative modeling.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness measures across 148 cortical regions (Destrieux atlas).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: In our analyses, we use cortical thickness measures estimated by Freesurfer version 5.3 or 6.0 over 148 cortical regions in the Destrieux atlas [57].; we set up four experimental settings for predicting the cortical thickness across 148 cortical regions

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age as covariate; sex as group-effect; scanner ids included as covariates for fixed-effect site modeling and as group-effect in HBR.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we use only age as a covariate except for the fixed-effect site modeling in which, by definition, the one-hot encoding of scanner ids are also included in the covariates. We use sex as a group-effect in all estimated models. In the HBR case, the scanner is also included as a group-effect.
